outputs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: preview-only world-map environment concept for a personal designer/frontend portfolio, NORMAL / IDLE state. One beautiful wide 16:9 illustration, not production UI.
Input images: Image 1 is a PALETTE / PAINTERLY MATERIAL / LIGHTING reference only; replace its small repetitive ruin architecture. Image 2 is a silhouette and material reference for the Contact lighthouse only.
Primary request: design one majestic bright sky world with exactly FOUR visibly different floating destination islands, using the approved warm pale limestone, sage/olive vegetation, clear blue sky, turquoise water and cool shaded rock. Monumental environment scale, confident broad hand-painted color planes and matte textures; restrained edge detail and natural consistent sunlight from upper left. Fantasy adventure environment appropriate to a thoughtful personal portfolio. Do not copy game characters, emblems or UI.
Composition: Projects is the largest landmark at upper middle/right, occupying about 40 percent of the image width. About is upper left at about half the Projects width. Skills sits lower middle-left. Contact sits lower right. Keep open blue-sky gaps between ALL four silhouettes and their cascading water. Just thin atmospheric cloud depth below, distant soft mountain silhouettes, no additional inhabited islands, no busy web of bridges, no character, no front-page header or buttons. Slightly elevated three-quarter camera with enough facade visible to read each island's function, shared horizon/perspective. Show island bottoms and falling water fully. The islands feel like substantial places, not cute tabletop miniatures.
PROJECTS: one enormous contemporary-in-fantasy exhibition bridge spanning TWO separated rugged cliff masses and a huge open chasm. The building is broad and horizontal, with a single long light stone roof, warm timber ceiling, open front, and four large recessed exhibition bays. A broad central stair and small railings show impressive scale. Exactly four large matte blank exhibition panels in the bays; pale paper surfaces and subtle timber frames, slightly angled toward visitor; no fabricated app UI, no invented project artwork, no logos. They visibly look like prepared art/design exhibition spaces even while idle, naturally illuminated but internal exhibit spotlights off. A substantial waterfall drops deep inside the central chasm, another short narrow cascade at one outside edge. Large empty sky beneath the spanning gallery is critical. No royal palace, castle, pagodas, turret towers or repeated small arches.
ABOUT: irregular forested ridge with an old spreading tree embracing a warm timber personal studio, low asymmetrical roofs and open deck, a real doorway, a desk visible behind glazing, planted footpath and tiny spring cascading over three natural rocks. Broad organic canopy silhouette, very little stone architecture.
SKILLS: long low open-sided timber workshop on a stepped split rock shelf. Exposed structural rafters, workbenches and a clearly readable large wooden waterwheel to one side, supplied from an elevated stone water trough and sluice. Two separate small spill streams beneath the wheel. Make this island functionally legible as a place of making. No grand mansion or arcaded palace.
CONTACT: slender tall limestone lighthouse with spiral exterior staircase, crescent harbor pool and low wooden pier, based on image 2. Small beacon lantern in daylight, no sweeping light beam yet. One thin long wind-blown waterfall from the curved harbor lip.
Text: only four small clean uppercase unboxed destination captions below their respective islands: "ABOUT", "SKILLS", "PROJECTS", "CONTACT". Keep each single caption well separated from artwork, dark desaturated blue readable against light cloud or sky. No other text.
Constraints: preserve bright midday palette, restrained saturation and broad shading. Vary geological bases: organic ridge, stepped shelf, split vertical cliffs, crescent harbor. The Projects building and its huge negative space are the primary focal point. Keep trees smaller on Projects to convey its architectural scale. Practical structural supports, stairs connect to doors, water flows from pools through actual outlets. No neon halos, glowing portals, giant smartphones, floating brand logos, decorative gold, sparkles, oversharpening, photoreal miniature/toy plastic, dense repetitive detail. This is an IMAGE DESIGN PREVIEW only.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: the HOVER / KEYBOARD FOCUS state paired to the supplied portfolio world-map NORMAL-state preview. This is the second still in a visual interaction storyboard, not a working website.
Edit target: the supplied complete four-island illustration. Preserve EXACT image dimensions and framing, all four island positions and sizes, geometry of rocks, buildings and trees, perspective, sky/cloud layout and all four existing labels. No extra islands, no changes to the number of exhibition panels. No cropping or zoom.
Change ONLY state-related lighting and a small physical movement of the four Projects exhibition panels:
1. PROJECTS is the active island. Its facade and rock faces gain clearly perceptible local contrast, luminous pale warm stone highlights and deeper cool shadow separation while retaining the SAME bright midday palette and matte material. The chasm must become deeper and more dimensional, not orange or neon. Existing four recessed exhibition bays switch on their focused warm-white downlights, visibly lighting the four blank cream display panels and making four discrete architectural pools of light on the gallery floor. Panels rotate slightly on slim physical vertical pivots, around 8–12 degrees toward the viewer, with credible supporting brackets; this is a small exhibition mechanism revealing the work, not flying holograms. Blank pale matte panels remain blank: no fake project UI, no invented screenshots/artwork/logos. Keep light confined to interior and immediate floor; no glowing island outline.
2. ABOUT, SKILLS and CONTACT maintain their shapes, labels and original colors but their island surfaces become slightly softer and less luminous, equivalent to a thin cool atmospheric veil and a modest reduction of contrast/exposure. They must remain clearly visible and attractive, not blacked out, blurred or grayscale. Preserve blue sky and cloud daylight unchanged, no global dark overlay and no evening conversion.
3. The existing PROJECTS text caption is modestly stronger in dark ink and has one thin underline as an additional active-state cue. Preserve exact label spelling and position. Other labels unchanged.
4. Water continues to look naturally flowing; no explosion, portal, fireworks, particles or energetic lightning.
Primary goal: immediately readable and tasteful selected-versus-idle contrast, grounded in gallery lights and physical exhibit movement. The hover image should match the normal image pixel composition closely so the user can compare. Do not add browser chrome, explanatory paragraphs, arrows, cursor, border or any new text.

proposedInteractions.about: Window shutters open slightly and interior/entry light comes on; spring remains ambient.
proposedInteractions.skills: Sluice opens slightly and waterwheel increases from slow ambient rotation; no game progression.
proposedInteractions.projects: Four exhibition downlights turn on and panels pivot slightly toward viewer; selected local contrast increases; surrounding islands are gently subdued.
proposedInteractions.contact: Beacon sweeps once and returns to gentle ambient rhythm; no flashing.

implementationNotes: Images are static concept keyframes, not working interactions or production assets.
Architecture, vegetation, moving water, mechanisms, lighting, labels and actual project images need separate production layers.
Four exhibition panels are deliberately blank: real project images should be inserted without AI repainting.
Hover and keyboard focus should share feedback; touch should offer explicit selection/entry.
With reduced motion or motion off, retain static selected lighting and label cue; omit mechanical movement.
No route, source code, existing production image or app documentation has been changed.
